text: **dsh-provider-usage**（DSH 插件，Web 与 Desktop 客户端）：在界面上集中查看已配置模型提供方的余额和用量配额。插件在主机侧发现提供方路由并查询对应额度接口，再通过侧边栏挂载可拖动的悬浮球和双语面板。它展示余额、订阅配额窗口、重置时间和当前使用中的提供方状态，也支持手动添加兼容提供方、调整刷新间隔与余额阈值。适合需要快速掌握多个模型账户余量的 DSH 用户；按各提供方配置使用凭据，Codex 等账户授权则沿用 DSH 凭据记录。

**dsh-provider-usage** (DSH Web/Desktop plugin): check provider balances and quotas. It detects configured routes, queries quota endpoints, and presents balances, usage windows, reset times, and the active provider in a draggable bilingual panel. Manual gateways and refresh settings are supported.

DSH 能不能自动识别已配置的模型服务并查额度？
给我一个能查看订阅用量窗口和剩余比例的界面。
Show me the remaining balance and quota for my configured model providers.
Can I see several AI provider usage limits in one DSH panel?
「提供方额度总览」：面板逐个列出已配置路由的余额或用量窗口，并显示查询状态与额度重置时间。打开悬浮球即可刷新查看。
「自动识别和手动添加提供方」：服务从当前 DSH 模型路由及其设置读取连接信息，也可用配置添加自定义网关；同 ID 的手动项会覆盖自动发现项。
「可拖动用量悬浮球」：Web 客户端把组件挂载到侧栏页脚，面板显示各提供方数据，并根据当前会话所用提供方更新状态提示。
「调整刷新与余额提醒」：用户可在面板选择刷新间隔；配置还提供刷新建议值及红黄余额阈值，便于按账户币种查看余量提示。
额度查询会访问各提供方的余额或配额接口；访问哪些外部服务取决于当前配置的模型路由。

English · 简体中文

dsh-provider-usage README · dsh-provider-usage：**Every provider's balance, one glance away.** A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that floats a small draggable usage ball over the Web GUI **and the Desktop app** — no more logging into each provider console to check whether you are about to run out of credit mid-session. One package supports both surfaces: the desktop window renders the same Web GUI, so the same install works everywhere.

dsh-provider-usage README · Features：- **Auto-detection** — enumerates the provider routes registered in the current profile (`ctx.llm`); zero configuration for well-known routes.
- **Per-kind wire adapters** — routes with no public balance/usage API (Google, Mistral, Groq, Bedrock, Azure, Qwen Token Plan, …) are listed as `unsupported` instead of being silently dropped:

dsh-provider-usage README · Features：| kind | routes | query | shows |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `deepseek` | `deepseek-official`, `deepseek` | `GET {baseURL}/user/balance` | total / granted / topped-up balance |
  | `deepseek-account` | `deepseek-account` (dsh ≥ 0.1.7) | `GET {platformOrigin}/api/v0/users/get_user_summary` | account wallet balance (recharge + bonus merged; **reads the harness's built-in DeepSeek Account sign-in**, zero config). The harness composes this route unconditionally, so the card is **omitted while no sign-in is stored** — it appears on the next poll after you sign in |
  | `moonshot` | `moonshotai-cn`, `moonshotai` | `GET {baseURL}/users/me/balance` | available / voucher / cash balance |
  | `kimi-coding` | `kimi-coding` | `GET {baseURL}/v1/usages` | 5h / weekly / monthly usage windows + reset countdown. A lapsed membership is reported as **“no active plan”** instead of a blank card — the endpoint answers `{}` (HTTP 200) once the plan ends |
  | `openrouter` | `openrouter` | `GET {origin}/api/v1/credits` | credits used / total |
  | `github-copilot` | `github-copilot` | `GET api.github.com/copilot_internal/user` | plan usage snapshots (paid) or monthly usag

dsh-provider-usage README · Provider setup guides：Most providers need nothing beyond their API key. Two families need one extra setup step:

dsh-provider-usage README · Provider setup guides：- **OpenAI Codex** — a ChatGPT-subscription provider authenticated by an OAuth grant in the harness credential store (no API key field). Route setup, token refresh/rotation behavior, and the intermittent "servers overloaded" retry policy: [docs/provider-codex.md](docs/provider-codex.md).
- **Volcengine Ark Agent Plan / Coding Plan** — plan quota lives on Volcengine's control plane and needs a signed IAM AK/SK pair in addition to the inference key. Route and credential setup: [docs/provider-ark.md](docs/provider-ark.md).

dsh-provider-usage README · Install or upgrade：> [!NOTE]
> Requires an existing [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) installation. Install and upgrade are the same command on every surface.

dsh-provider-usage README · Web GUI：After changing the plugin set, restart `dsh web` and refresh the page (later code-only changes need just a rebuild + re-add + refresh). If the release you want was published very recently, your profile's supply-chain cooldown (`minimumReleaseAge`) may silently keep the older version — pin the exact version instead (`dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-provider-usage@0.3.10`) and dsh will exempt it automatically. The version badge in the panel header confirms which release is actually loaded.

dsh-provider-usage README · Desktop app：The same package also runs in the Desktop app — the desktop window renders the same Web GUI, so **no separate plugin or build is needed**. The desktop app owns its own profile (`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`), so install the plugin there once:

dsh-provider-usage README · Desktop app：1. In the desktop app, open **Settings → Plugins** → **Add plugin** → **Install a third-party plugin** ([screenshot](docs/desktop-install-menu-en.png)).
2. Enter `dsh-provider-usage` and click **Install** ([screenshot](docs/desktop-install-dialog-en.png)).
3. Click **Enable now** ([screenshot](docs/desktop-install-enable-en.png)).

dsh-provider-usage README · Desktop app：The floating ball appears in the desktop window immediately ([screenshot](docs/desktop-panel-en.png)). Panel preferences (ball position, refresh interval, thresholds) persist per origin, so the desktop app and the Web GUI keep their own layouts independently.

To upgrade on the Desktop app, uninstall then reinstall from the same Plugins page (the desktop dialog asks for this order) and reload the window.

dsh-provider-usage README · Desktop app：CLI alternative: fully quit the desktop app (including the tray), then use the CLI carried by the desktop installation — `<install-dir>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd plugin --profile desktop add dsh-provider-usage@latest`. The npm-installed `dsh` refuses the reserved `desktop` profile (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`).

dsh-provider-usage README · Build from source：```sh
git clone https://github.com/lizhouai/dsh-provider-usage.git
cd dsh-provider-usage
pnpm install
pnpm build

dsh-provider-usage README · Build from source：Install the **tarball**, not the repo directory: `dsh plugin --profile web add .` links the repo, whose own `node_modules` then shadows the harness's shared `@deepseek-ai/cordis` instance and the host half never registers (RPC 404). The link form is still handy for client-only UI iteration — the browser bundle is self-contained, so a rebuild + page refresh picks it up — but switch to the tarball (or the npm release) whenever you need the host half. If pnpm fails with `EPERM ... symlink` while replacing a linked install, delete the stale `node_modules/dsh-provider-usage` junction in the profile directory and retry.

dsh-provider-usage README · Host compatibility：The host packages this plugin imports (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-credentials`, `-settings`, `-typert-protocol`, `-launch-environment`) resolve to the running harness's own copies, and dsh's peer gate compares the declared ranges against the runtime version. This plugin therefore declares an **open lower bound** (`>=0.1.2-alpha.3`), which every runtime passes — a narrow `^`-range would be skipped as `skipping profile bundle` on each dsh minor release. Install through `dsh plugin … add` (pnpm-based): plain `npm install` answers `ERESOLVE`, because standard semver never matches a prerelease against an open range.

dsh-provider-usage README · Host compatibility：If a dsh release renames a seam the plugin reads, the plugin degrades instead of breaking — the harness log names what is missing (`provider-usage: this dsh provides no …`, see `src/host-seams.ts`), and the [`compat`](.github/workflows/compat.yml) workflow replays the gate against the `latest` and `next` release lines daily, so drift surfaces in CI rather than in your panel.

dsh-provider-usage README · Configuration：Defaults work out of the box: the plugin auto-detects every provider route of the active profile. A trusted profile can tune behavior in its bundle patch — `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (desktop: `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`) — **override the bundle's row by id** (the package's own bundle patch already inserts it; a second `insert` of the same id fails the boot with `duplicate loader entry id`):

dsh-provider-usage README · Configuration：```yaml
- id: provider-usage
  name: dsh-provider-usage
  config:
    refreshSeconds: 60          # suggested panel refresh interval (5–86400)

dsh-provider-usage README · Configuration：| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `refreshSeconds` | number | `60` | Suggested widget refresh interval in seconds (5–86400) |
| `balanceRedThreshold` | number | `10` | Balance below this amount turns red, compared in the balance's own currency |
| `balanceYellowThreshold` | number | `30` | Balance below this amount turns yellow, compared in the balance's own currency |
| `autoDetect` | boolean | `true` | Enumerate live provider routes from the llm registry |
| `queryTimeoutMs` | number | `20000` | Per-attempt query timeout (1000–120000); each retry gets a fresh timeout |
| `queryRetries` | number | `2` | Retries for transient errors — timeout / network / HTTP 408, 425, 429, 5xx (0–10); permanent 4xx errors fail immediately |
| `queryRetryDelayMs` | number | `2000` | Base delay between retries (100–60000), doubled per attempt, capped at 10s |
| `providers` | array | `[]` | Manual provider specs: `{id, kind, baseURL, apiKeyEnv, displayName?, enabled?}`; `kind` is one of the adapter table above |
dsh-provider-usage README · Configuration：The same fields can be hot-updated under the `provider-usage:` namespace in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`.

dsh-provider-usage README · Adding a manual provider：```yaml
config:
  providers:
    - id: my-deepseek-gateway
      kind: deepseek

dsh-provider-usage README · How it works：- **Host half** (`src/index.ts`): `UsageService extends TypertRemoteService` exposes `usage/list` via the `Remote('list')` marker, applied without decorator syntax (SRC mode, no codegen). Config is declared with schemastery, and the settings provider's `installSection` enables hot updates from the settings document.
- **Client half** (`src/client/`): a `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})` bundle (built by tsdown) mounts through the `sidebar.footer.action` slot (used purely as a mount point — the trigger itself is a floating ball portaled to `document.body`) and polls `usage/list` through `ctx.connection.rpc.call('/api', 'usage/list', {args:{}})` on its own interval. The service stays stateless — every poll fetches live values.
